question: To which Hindustani music Gharana are the Gundecha brothers related?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Dagari Gharana.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Gundecha Brothers (Ramakant Gundecha and Umakant Gundecha) are eminent Indian classical vocalists renowned for singing Dhrupad in the Dagar Gharana (Dagarvani) style. (डागर घराना — गुंडेचा बंधु)

 

• They were trained by Ustad Zia Fariduddin Dagar, a leading exponent of the Dagarvani tradition of Dhrupad, and later carried the tradition forward through performances and teaching, including founding the Dhrupad Sansthan in Bhopal.

 

• Dhrupad is considered the oldest surviving form of Hindustani classical vocal music, characterized by its austere, meditative style and use of the pakhawaj as accompaniment.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other gharanas mentioned relate mainly to khyal singing: the Agra Gharana (founded by Haji Sujan Khan), the Patiala Gharana (associated with Bade Ghulam Ali Khan) and the Indore Gharana (associated with Amir Khan).

 

NOTE

 

• Agra Gharana (Option 2): A khyal gharana known for its powerful, masculine style of singing, distinct from the Dagar Gharana's Dhrupad tradition.

 

• Patiala Gharana (Option 3): A khyal gharana founded by Ali Baksh and Fateh Ali Khan, famous for its intricate taans.

 

• Indore Gharana (Option 4): A relatively younger khyal gharana associated with Ustad Amir Khan.

question: When and where did the first Asian Games take place?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1951, New Delhi.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The first Asian Games were held in New Delhi in 1951, from 4 to 11 March, inaugurated by then President Rajendra Prasad. (प्रथम एशियाई खेल — नई दिल्ली, 1951)

 

• The Games were organised under the Asian Games Federation (predecessor of the Olympic Council of Asia), founded on the initiative of Guru Dutt Sondhi.

 

• 11 countries participated in the 1951 Asian Games, competing in 6 sports disciplines.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• India has hosted the Asian Games twice — 1951 and 1982, both in New Delhi.

 

• The Asian Games are held every 4 years; the 2023 edition (19th Asian Games) was held in Hangzhou, China.

 

NOTE

 

• 1982, Punjab (Option 2): India hosted the 9th Asian Games in 1982, but in New Delhi, not Punjab.

 

• 2014, Maharashtra (Option 3): The 17th Asian Games were held in Incheon, South Korea in 2014, not in India.

 

• 2010, New Delhi (Option 4): New Delhi hosted the 2010 Commonwealth Games, not the Asian Games; the 2010 Asian Games (16th edition) were held in Guangzhou, China.

question: The Battle of Khanua was fought between Babur and ________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Rana Sanga.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Battle of Khanwa was fought on 17 March 1527 between Babur and Rana Sanga (Maharana Sangram Singh) of Mewar. (खानवा का युद्ध — राणा सांगा)

 

• Babur's decisive victory at Khanwa, near Fatehpur Sikri (Rajasthan), consolidated Mughal power in northern India after his earlier victory at the First Battle of Panipat (1526) against Ibrahim Lodi.

 

• Babur assumed the title 'Ghazi' after this victory over the Rajput confederacy led by Rana Sanga.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Babur founded the Mughal Empire in India in 1526 after defeating Ibrahim Lodi at the First Battle of Panipat.

 

• Rana Sanga died shortly after the Battle of Khanwa, in 1528.

 

NOTE

 

• Medini Rao (Option 1): A Rajput chieftain of Malwa who was defeated by Babur at the Battle of Chanderi (1528), not Khanwa.

 

• Maharana Pratap (Option 2): A later ruler of Mewar, famous for the Battle of Haldighati (1576) against Mughal emperor Akbar.

 

• Rana Ratna Singh (Option 3): Also spelled Ratan Singh, was a ruler of Mewar associated with the legend of Padmini and the siege by Alauddin Khilji, not connected to Babur's Battle of Khanwa.

question: Which of the following pairs of Indian rivers is west flowing?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Narmada and Tapi.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Narmada and Tapi (Tapti) are the two major west-flowing rivers of peninsular India, both draining into the Arabian Sea through rift valleys. (नर्मदा और तापी — पश्चिम की ओर बहने वाली नदियाँ)

 

• The Narmada River originates at Amarkantak in Madhya Pradesh and flows through Madhya Pradesh, Maharashtra and Gujarat before entering the Gulf of Khambhat (Cambay).

 

• The Tapi River originates near Multai in the Betul district of Madhya Pradesh and flows through Madhya Pradesh, Maharashtra and Gujarat, emptying into the Gulf of Khambhat.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Most major peninsular rivers (Mahanadi, Godavari, Krishna, Kaveri) flow eastward into the Bay of Bengal, as peninsular India tilts from west to east.

 

• Other minor west-flowing rivers include the Sabarmati, Mahi, Luni and several short streams of the Western Ghats.

 

NOTE

 

• Mahanadi and Godavari (Option 1): Both are east-flowing rivers that drain into the Bay of Bengal.

 

• Krishna and Kaveri (Option 2): Both are east-flowing rivers that drain into the Bay of Bengal.

 

• Mahanadi and Krishna (Option 3): Both are east-flowing rivers that drain into the Bay of Bengal.

question: Any citizen of India can make a declaration renouncing his/her Indian citizenship under the ________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Citizenship Act, 1955.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Under Section 8 of the Citizenship Act, 1955, any citizen of India of full age and capacity can make a declaration renouncing his/her Indian citizenship. (नागरिकता अधिनियम, 1955 — नागरिकता त्याग)

 

• Once the declaration is registered by the prescribed authority, the person ceases to be an Indian citizen; if the declarant is male, minor children also cease to be citizens unless they later elect to resume it on attaining majority.

 

• The Citizenship Act, 1955 governs the acquisition and determination of Indian citizenship through birth, descent, registration, naturalisation and incorporation of territory, along with renunciation (Section 8), termination (Section 9) and deprivation (Section 10).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Act has been amended several times, notably by the Citizenship (Amendment) Act, 2003 (introducing OCI) and the Citizenship (Amendment) Act, 2019.

 

NOTE

 

• Citizenship Act, 1975 (Option 1): No such standalone citizenship legislation exists; India's citizenship law of that era continued to be governed by the 1955 Act.

 

• Citizenship Act, 1985 (Option 2): No such Act exists; 1985 saw the Assam Accord, not a new citizenship statute.

 

• Citizenship Act, 1965 (Option 4): No such Act exists; this is not a real citizenship legislation year.

question: El Nino is a climate pattern that describes the unusual warming of surface waters in which ocean?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Pacific Ocean.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• El Niño is a climate pattern characterised by the unusual warming of surface waters in the central and eastern equatorial Pacific Ocean. (एल नीनो — प्रशांत महासागर)

 

• It is part of the El Niño-Southern Oscillation (ENSO) cycle and typically weakens the Indian monsoon, often leading to below-normal rainfall in India.

 

• El Niño occurs irregularly, roughly every 2 to 7 years, and its opposite phase (cooling of the same waters) is called La Niña.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The term 'El Niño' (Spanish for 'the little boy'/Christ child) was originally used by Peruvian fishermen to describe the warm current appearing around Christmas.

 

• ENSO-neutral, El Niño and La Niña conditions are monitored by agencies like NOAA and the India Meteorological Department (IMD).

 

NOTE

 

• Indian Ocean (Option 1): Its own warming/cooling phenomenon is called the Indian Ocean Dipole (IOD), distinct from El Niño.

 

• Atlantic Ocean (Option 2): Has an analogous but distinct phenomenon called the Atlantic Niño.

 

• Arctic Ocean (Option 3): Not associated with El Niño; it is affected by separate polar climate processes.

question:
With reference to Chethiagiri Vihar festival consider the following statements and select the correct option.

i) It is a Buddhist festival.

ii) It is held at Sanchi, Madhya Pradesh.

iii) Relics of SariPutta and Maha Moggallana are worshiped.
solution_text:
The correct answer is i, ii, iii.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Chethiyagiri Vihar Festival is an annual Buddhist festival held at Sanchi, Madhya Pradesh, organised to venerate the sacred relics of Sariputta and Maha Moggallana, the two chief disciples of Gautam Buddha. (चेतियागिरी विहार महोत्सव — सांची, मध्य प्रदेश)

 

• Statement i is correct: It is celebrated as a major Buddhist festival, drawing monks and devotees from across the world.

 

• Statement ii is correct: The festival is held at Chethiyagiri Vihara in Sanchi, near Bhopal in Madhya Pradesh, home to the famous Sanchi Stupa complex.

 

• Statement iii is correct: During the festival, the relics of Sariputta and Maha Moggallana — originally excavated from Sanchi's stupas and later returned to India from London — are taken out for public veneration.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Sanchi Stupa was commissioned by Emperor Ashoka in the 3rd century BCE and is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

 

• The relics of Sariputta and Moggallana were originally sent to England in the 19th century and were ceremonially returned to India in 1952, since when they have been enshrined and displayed periodically at Sanchi's Chetiyagiri Vihara.

 

NOTE

 

• Options 1, 2 and 3 (Both i and iii / Both ii and iii / Both i and ii): Each of these is incorrect because it omits at least one of the three statements, all of which are, in fact, factually correct.

question: Formulas in MS-Excel always start with which of the following symbols?
solution_text:
The correct answer is =.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• In Microsoft Excel, every formula must begin with an equals sign (=), which signals to Excel that the content of the cell is a formula and not plain text or a number. (सूत्र चिह्न — बराबर का चिन्ह)

 

• After the '=' sign, formulas can include **cell references, operators (+, -, *, /), functions (e.g., SUM, AVERAGE)** and constants, e.g. `=A1+B1` or `=SUM(A1:A10)`.

 

• If a formula is typed without the leading '=', Excel treats the entry as plain text rather than evaluating it as a calculation.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Excel formulas can also begin with a plus (+) or minus (-) sign in some legacy contexts (inherited from Lotus 1-2-3 compatibility), but Excel automatically converts these to start with '=' upon entry.

 

NOTE

 

• == (Option 1): Not a valid formula starter in Excel; a double equals sign is not recognised as initiating a formula.

 

• - (Option 2): A minus sign alone does not properly initiate a standard Excel formula reference.

 

• ! (Option 3): The exclamation mark is used in Excel to separate a sheet name from a cell reference (e.g., Sheet1!A1), not to start a formula.

question: In August 2021, the Administrator of Lakshadweep, Praful Khoda Patel, highlighted that __________ style water villas, a project which is a first of its kind, will soon be set up in Lakshadweep, at a cost of 800 crores, in a bid to attract tourists to scenic beauty of the Union Territory.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Maldives.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• In August 2021, the then Administrator of Lakshadweep, Praful Khoda Patel, announced plans for Maldives-style floating/water villas to be developed in Lakshadweep at a cost of around ₹800 crore, aimed at boosting tourism. (मालदीव शैली — लक्षद्वीप जल विला)

 

• The initiative was part of a broader push to develop Lakshadweep's tourism infrastructure, drawing inspiration from the overwater bungalows popularised by the Maldives.

 

• Lakshadweep is India's smallest Union Territory, comprising a group of 36 islands (of which about 10 are inhabited) in the Arabian Sea, with Kavaratti as its capital.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Lakshadweep gained wider tourism attention in January 2024 after Prime Minister Narendra Modi's visit and subsequent promotion of the islands as a tourist destination.

 

NOTE

 

• Mexico (Option 1): Not known for the overwater water-villa style of tourism infrastructure referenced here.

 

• Fiji (Option 3): Also has overwater bungalows, but the announcement specifically referenced the Maldives model.

 

• Malaysia (Option 4): Not the country referenced in this announcement.

question: In which year did a trio of scientists, Avery, MacLeod and McCarty, prove that except viruses, all living organisms have DNA as their genetic material?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1944.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• In 1944, Oswald Avery, Colin MacLeod and Maclyn McCarty conducted experiments building on Frederick Griffith's earlier work, demonstrating that DNA (deoxyribonucleic acid), not protein, is the genetic material responsible for transformation in bacteria (Pneumococcus). (एवरी-मैकलियोड-मैकार्टी प्रयोग — 1944)

 

• Their experiment showed that purified DNA extracted from a virulent (smooth) strain of bacteria could transform a non-virulent (rough) strain into a virulent one, proving DNA carries hereditary information.

 

• This finding was pivotal in shifting the scientific consensus away from the earlier belief that proteins were the genetic material, paving the way for Watson and Crick's 1953 discovery of the DNA double helix structure.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Frederick Griffith's 1928 transformation experiment with Pneumococcus bacteria first hinted at a 'transforming principle,' which Avery, MacLeod and McCarty later identified as DNA.

 

NOTE

 

• 1918 (Option 1): Predates this discovery; no major DNA-related breakthrough occurred in this year relevant to this experiment.

 

• 1902 (Option 2): This is much earlier and unrelated; Walter Sutton and Theodor Boveri's chromosome theory of heredity dates to around this period, not this specific DNA experiment.

 

• 1961 (Option 4): This is later; by this time DNA's role was already well established (Watson-Crick 1953), and the genetic code was being deciphered (Nirenberg and Matthaei, 1961).

question:
Which of the following statements is/are correct?

I- Radio broadcasting started in India in 1923 by the Radio Club of Bombay.

II- All India Radio came into being in 1936.

III - In 1976, TV was delinked from All India Radio (AIR) and got a separate identity as Door darshan (DD).
option_1: I, II and III are correct
option_2: Both I and II are correct.
option_3: Both II and III are correct.
solution_text:
The correct answer is I, II and III are correct.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• All three statements about the history of radio and television broadcasting in India are correct. (आकाशवाणी और दूरदर्शन — प्रसारण इतिहास)

 

• Statement I is correct: Radio broadcasting in India began in 1923 when the Radio Club of Bombay made the first-ever broadcast, followed shortly by radio clubs in Calcutta and Madras.

 

• Statement II is correct: The Indian State Broadcasting Service was renamed All India Radio (AIR) in 1936, and it later adopted the name Akashvani in 1957.

 

• Statement III is correct: In 1976, television services were delinked from All India Radio and given a separate, independent identity as Doordarshan (DD).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Television broadcasting in India began experimentally in 1959 in Delhi, under All India Radio, before eventually becoming Doordarshan in 1976.

 

• Doordarshan launched its first satellite channel, DD National, and has since expanded into numerous regional and specialised channels.

 

NOTE

 

• Both I and II are correct (Option 2): Incorrect because it wrongly excludes Statement III, which is also factually correct.

 

• Both II and III are correct (Option 3): Incorrect because it wrongly excludes Statement I, which is also factually correct.

 

• Only III is correct (Option 4): Incorrect because it wrongly excludes Statements I and II, both of which are factually correct.

question: In which year was the Rajiv Gandhi Khel Ratna award renamed as Major Dhyan Chand Khel Ratna award, which is the highest sporting honour in the nation?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 2021.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Rajiv Gandhi Khel Ratna award, India's highest sporting honour, was renamed the Major Dhyan Chand Khel Ratna award in August 2021, ahead of National Sports Day. (मेजर ध्यानचंद खेल रत्न — 2021)

 

• The renaming was announced by Prime Minister Narendra Modi, honouring hockey legend Major Dhyan Chand, widely known as the 'Wizard of Hockey.'

 

• The award recognises the most outstanding performance in the field of sports over a four-year period and carries a medal, certificate and a cash prize.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• National Sports Day is observed on 29 August every year, marking the birth anniversary of Major Dhyan Chand.

 

• Other sporting honours in India include the Arjuna Award, Dronacharya Award (for coaches) and Padma Awards.

 

NOTE

 

• 2014 (Option 1): Not the year of renaming; the award was still called the Rajiv Gandhi Khel Ratna at this time.

 

• 1991 (Option 3): This is the year the Rajiv Gandhi Khel Ratna award was originally instituted, not when it was renamed.

 

• 2019 (Option 4): Not the correct year; the renaming took place in 2021.

question: Which of these is NOT true of the second phase of the green revolution?
option_1: It was adopted by farmers living in dry and semi-arid regions of India.
option_2: It covered the period of the 1980s.
option_3: It covered the period of the 1960s and 1970s.
option_4: It was launched in areas with a significant shift from dry to wet (irrigated) cultivation.
solution_text:
The correct answer is It covered the period of the 1960s and 1970s.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The statement that the second phase of the Green Revolution 'covered the period of the 1960s and 1970s' is NOT true — that period corresponds to the first phase of the Green Revolution, not the second. (हरित क्रांति — द्वितीय चरण, 1980 का दशक)

 

• The first phase (mid-1960s to late 1970s) was largely confined to irrigated, resource-rich regions like Punjab, Haryana and western Uttar Pradesh, focused mainly on wheat.

 

• The second phase (1980s) extended the Green Revolution to dry and semi-arid regions of India and to crops beyond wheat, benefitting states such as those in central and southern India.

 

• The second phase was also marked by a shift in some areas from purely dry farming toward more irrigated cultivation practices, expanding the scope of high-yielding variety technology.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Green Revolution in India is credited to agricultural scientist M. S. Swaminathan, often called the 'Father of the Green Revolution in India,' along with the contribution of Norman Borlaug's high-yielding wheat varieties.

 

• The Green Revolution significantly boosted India's foodgrain production, helping the country move toward self-sufficiency after decades of food shortages.

 

NOTE

 

• It was adopted by farmers living in dry and semi-arid regions of India (Option 1): This is TRUE of the second phase, so it is not the answer to this 'NOT true' question.

 

• It covered the period of the 1980s (Option 2): This is TRUE of the second phase, so it is not the answer.

 

• It was launched in areas with a significant shift from dry to wet (irrigated) cultivation (Option 4): This is TRUE of the second phase, so it is not the answer.

question: Where was the first Durand Cup, India’s oldest football tournament, held?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Shimla.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Durand Cup, India's oldest football tournament and one of the oldest in the world, was first held in 1888 in Shimla. (डूरंड कप — शिमला, 1888)

 

• It was instituted by Sir Mortimer Durand, the then Foreign Secretary of British India, after whom the tournament is named.

 

• The tournament is organised by the Durand Football Tournament Society, with patronage historically from the Indian Army; it now typically features matches across cities including Kolkata.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Durand Cup is the third oldest football tournament in the world, after the FA Cup (England) and the Scottish Cup.

 

• In recent years, the tournament has been held primarily in Kolkata, along with venues like Guwahati and Shillong.

 

NOTE

 

• Madras (Option 1): Not the venue of the first Durand Cup.

 

• Calcutta (Option 3): Calcutta is closely associated with hosting the tournament in modern times, but the tournament originated in Shimla, not Calcutta.

 

• Delhi (Option 4): Not the venue of the first edition, though the tournament was later shifted to Delhi for several decades in the 20th century.

question: The UIDAI is under the jurisdiction of which of the following ministries?
option_2: Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology
solution_text:
The correct answer is Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Unique Identification Authority of India (UIDAI), which issues the Aadhaar number, functions under the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY). (यूआईडीएआई — इलेक्ट्रॉनिकी और सूचना प्रौद्योगिकी मंत्रालय)

 

• UIDAI was established in January 2009 and was earlier attached to the Planning Commission; it was placed under MeitY following the enactment of the Aadhaar (Targeted Delivery of Financial and Other Subsidies, Benefits and Services) Act, 2016.

 

• UIDAI's core mandate is to issue Aadhaar numbers to residents of India and to maintain and update the associated demographic and biometric data.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• The first Aadhaar number was issued in 2010 to a resident of Nandurbar, Maharashtra.

 

• As of recent years, Aadhaar has become one of the world's largest biometric identity systems, covering over a billion residents.

 

NOTE

 

• Ministry of Finance (Option 1): Not the administering ministry for UIDAI, though Aadhaar is widely used for financial inclusion (e.g., linking with bank accounts, DBT).

 

• Ministry of Home Affairs (Option 3): Not responsible for UIDAI; it primarily deals with internal security, police and Census-related matters.

 

• Ministry of Education (Option 4): Not related to UIDAI's administration.

question: In which year was Micro Units Development and Refinance Agency (MUDRA) introduced?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 2015.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Micro Units Development and Refinance Agency (MUDRA) was launched by Prime Minister Narendra Modi on 8 April 2015 as part of the Pradhan Mantri MUDRA Yojana (PMMY). (मुद्रा योजना — 2015)

 

• MUDRA provides refinance support to banks/NBFCs/MFIs for lending to non-corporate, non-farm small/micro enterprises, with loans up to ₹10 lakh (later enhanced under the Tarun Plus category).

 

• Loans under the scheme are categorised into three types based on the stage of business growth: Shishu (up to ₹50,000), Kishor (₹50,000 to ₹5 lakh) and Tarun (₹5 lakh to ₹10 lakh).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• MUDRA loans are collateral-free, aimed particularly at supporting small entrepreneurs, especially in the informal sector, including women entrepreneurs.

 

• The scheme falls under the broader financial inclusion initiatives alongside Pradhan Mantri Jan Dhan Yojana and Stand-Up India.

 

NOTE

 

• 2017, 2013, 2009 (Options 1, 2, 3): None of these correspond to MUDRA's actual launch year; the agency and the associated Yojana were both launched in 2015.

question: Which shortcut key is used to paste a slide in Microsoft PowerPoint?
solution_text:
The correct answer is CTRL + V.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• In Microsoft PowerPoint (and most Windows applications), CTRL + V is the standard keyboard shortcut used to paste content — such as a copied or cut slide, text, or object — from the clipboard. (पेस्ट शॉर्टकट — CTRL + V)

 

• The paste shortcut works in conjunction with CTRL + C (copy) and CTRL + X (cut), together forming the standard clipboard operations across Microsoft Office applications.

 

• To paste a slide specifically, a user can copy/cut a slide from the slide panel and then use CTRL + V at the desired location within the slide sequence.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other common PowerPoint shortcuts include F5 (start slideshow from beginning), CTRL + M (new slide) and CTRL + D (duplicate slide).

 

NOTE

 

• CTRL + C (Option 1): Used to copy selected content, not paste it.

 

• CTRL + P (Option 2): Used to open the Print dialog box, not to paste.

 

• CTRL + X (Option 4): Used to cut selected content, not paste it.

question: In the Hindustani music system, the ________ are allotted to different hours of the day and different seasons.
solution_text:
The correct answer is ragas.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• In the Hindustani classical music system, ragas are traditionally allotted to specific hours of the day (prahars) and seasons (ritus), based on the belief that certain melodic moods resonate best at particular times. (राग — समय और ऋतु का बंधन)

 

• For example, Raga Bhairav is traditionally sung in the early morning, Raga Yaman in the evening, and Raga Malhar is associated with the monsoon season.

 

• This system of time-and-season allocation is known as 'samay-siddhanta' and is a distinctive feature of Hindustani music, though less rigidly followed in Carnatic music.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• A raga is a melodic framework built on a specific set of notes (swaras), with defined ascending (aroha) and descending (avaroha) patterns, and characteristic phrases.

 

• Ragas are broadly grouped into thaats (parent scales), a classification system formalised by musicologist V. N. Bhatkhande.

 

NOTE

 

• Gita (Option 1): Refers generally to a song or devotional composition, not the time/season-based melodic framework being described.

 

• Varnas (Option 2): In the context of Carnatic music, varnams are specific compositional forms used for practice, not linked to hour/season allocation.

 

• Srutis (Option 3): Refer to the smallest, precise intervals of pitch/microtones in Indian classical music theory, not the time-of-day/season classification.

question: Which organisation was started in the Pune district of Maharashtra in the 1870s with the aim of promoting education and social rights among the underprivileged group of the society?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Satyashodhak Samaj.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Satyashodhak Samaj ('Society of Truth Seekers') was founded by Jyotirao Phule in Pune, Maharashtra, in 1873, with the aim of promoting education and social rights among the underprivileged, particularly the lower castes and women. (सत्यशोधक समाज — ज्योतिराव फुले, पुणे 1873)

 

• The organisation campaigned against caste discrimination, Brahmanical dominance and social inequality, and promoted widow remarriage, women's education and rights for peasants and lower-caste communities.

 

• Jyotirao Phule, along with his wife Savitribai Phule, is also credited with opening some of the first schools for girls and for lower-caste students in India.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Jyotirao Phule was honoured with the title 'Mahatma' by the people of Maharashtra for his social reform work.

 

• The Satyashodhak Samaj's ideology later influenced subsequent social reform and anti-caste movements in Maharashtra, including the work of B. R. Ambedkar.

 

NOTE

 

• Deepalaya Samaj (Option 2): Not a historical 1870s social reform organisation from Pune; not associated with this movement.

 

• Shoshit Seva Samaj (Option 3): Not the organisation founded in Pune in the 1870s for this purpose.

 

• Prarthana Samaj (Option 4): Founded in Bombay in 1867 by Atmaram Pandurang (with later leadership from Mahadev Govind Ranade), it was a distinct reformist religious organisation, not the one described here.

question:
Match the dances in column A with their states in column B.

Column A (Dances): 1. Bharatanatyam  2. Mohiniattam  3. Garba  4. Sattriya

Column B (States): a. Gujarat  b. Tamil Nadu  c. Kerala  d. Assam
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1-b, 2-c, 3-a, 4-d.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Bharatanatyam originated in and is closely associated with Tamil Nadu (1-b). (भरतनाट्यम — तमिलनाडु)

 

• Mohiniattam is a classical dance form of Kerala (2-c), known for its graceful, swaying movements.

 

• Garba is a traditional folk dance of Gujarat (3-a), performed especially during Navratri.

 

• Sattriya is the classical dance form of Assam (4-d), originating in the Vaishnavite monasteries (sattras) established by Srimanta Sankardev.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• India has eight classical dance forms recognised by the Sangeet Natak Akademi: Bharatanatyam, Kathak, Kathakali, Kuchipudi, Odissi, Manipuri, Mohiniyattam and Sattriya.

 

• Sattriya was accorded classical dance status in 2000, the most recent addition to this list.

 

NOTE

 

• 1-c, 2-b, 3-a, 4-d (Option 1): Incorrectly swaps the states of Bharatanatyam and Mohiniattam.

 

• 1-a, 2-c, 3-b, 4-d (Option 2): Incorrectly pairs Bharatanatyam with Gujarat and Garba with Tamil Nadu.

 

• 1-b, 2-c, 3-d, 4-a (Option 3): Incorrectly pairs Garba with Assam and Sattriya with Gujarat.

question: Who proposed that ‘Light is made up of waves propagating perpendicular to the direction of its movement’?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Huygens.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Christiaan Huygens, a Dutch physicist, proposed the wave theory of light, describing light as a wave phenomenon propagating through a medium, in contrast to Newton's corpuscular (particle) theory. (ह्यूजेंस — प्रकाश का तरंग सिद्धांत)

 

• Huygens presented his theory in his 'Treatise on Light' (Traité de la Lumière), published in 1690, introducing what is now known as Huygens' Principle, describing how every point on a wavefront acts as a source of secondary wavelets.

 

• His wave theory successfully explained phenomena such as reflection and refraction, laying important groundwork for the later, more complete transverse-wave understanding of light developed by scientists such as Young and Fresnel.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Isaac Newton proposed the rival corpuscular (particle) theory of light, which dominated scientific thought until wave-based explanations gained wider acceptance in the 19th century.

 

• The wave nature of light was later firmly established through the work of Thomas Young (interference, 1801) and Augustin-Jean Fresnel, and light's electromagnetic nature was subsequently unified by James Clerk Maxwell.

 

NOTE

 

• Newton (Option 1): Proposed the corpuscular (particle) theory of light, viewing light as a stream of tiny particles, not as waves.

 

• Kepler (Option 3): Known for his laws of planetary motion, not for a wave theory of light.

 

• Pauli (Option 4): A 20th-century physicist known for the Pauli Exclusion Principle in quantum mechanics, unrelated to classical wave theories of light.

question: Balasaraswati who was regarded as child prodigy by Vidhwans and Pandits played an important role in reviving the dance form ______________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Bharatanatyam.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• T. Balasaraswati, regarded as a child prodigy by vidwans (scholars) and pandits, was one of the most celebrated exponents of Bharatanatyam and played a pivotal role in reviving and popularising the dance form in the 20th century. (बालासरस्वती — भरतनाट्यम)

 

• She belonged to a traditional family of devadasi dancers and musicians from Tamil Nadu and made her solo debut at the age of seven.

 

• Balasaraswati is especially known for her performance of the abhinaya (expressive) elements of Bharatanatyam, and she was awarded the Padma Bhushan (1977) and the Sangeet Natak Akademi Award.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Balasaraswati performed internationally and helped bring Bharatanatyam global recognition, including notable performances in the United States.

 

• She belonged to a lineage that included renowned Carnatic musicians, being the great-granddaughter of the composer Veena Dhanammal.

 

NOTE

 

• Kuchipudi (Option 1): A classical dance form of Andhra Pradesh, not associated with Balasaraswati's revival work.

 

• Mohiniyattam (Option 2): A classical dance form of Kerala, distinct from Balasaraswati's field of Bharatanatyam.

 

• Kathak (Option 4): A classical dance form associated with North India, unrelated to Balasaraswati.

question: Which of the following statements about the Mahila Samman Savings Certificate is incorrect as of 31 March 2024?
option_1: The tenure of the scheme is 5 years.
option_2: The scheme is valid up to 31 March 2025.
option_3: The scheme was announced in the 2023-24 budget.
option_4: The maximum limit of deposit in the scheme is 2 lakhs per year.
solution_text:
The correct answer is The tenure of the scheme is 5 years.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The statement 'The tenure of the scheme is 5 years' is incorrect — the Mahila Samman Savings Certificate (MSSC) actually has a tenure of 2 years from the date of opening the account. (महिला सम्मान बचत प्रमाण पत्र — 2 वर्ष अवधि)

 

• The scheme was announced in the Union Budget 2023-24 by Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman, as a one-time small savings scheme for women and girls.

 

• Deposits under the scheme could be made up to 31 March 2025, with a maximum deposit limit of ₹2 lakh and a fixed interest rate of 7.5% per annum, with partial withdrawal facility available.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• MSSC accounts can be opened at post offices and authorised public/private sector banks, in the name of a woman or on behalf of a minor girl by her guardian.

 

• The scheme offers partial withdrawal of up to 40% of the eligible balance after one year from the date of account opening.

 

NOTE

 

• The scheme is valid up to 31 March 2025 (Option 2): This statement is correct — the scheme's deposit window was open until this date.

 

• The scheme was announced in the 2023-24 budget (Option 3): This statement is correct — it was announced by the Finance Minister in the Union Budget 2023-24.

 

• The maximum limit of deposit in the scheme is 2 lakhs per year (Option 4): This statement reflects the scheme's ₹2 lakh maximum deposit limit and is treated as correct here.

question: As per the Economic Survey 2022-23, the Labour Force Participation Rate for males has gone up to ________in 2020-21.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 57.5%.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• As per the Economic Survey 2022-23, the Labour Force Participation Rate (LFPR) for males rose to 57.5% in 2020-21, based on data from the Periodic Labour Force Survey (PLFS). (श्रम बल भागीदारी दर — पुरुष, 2020-21)

 

• LFPR measures the proportion of the population (aged 15 years and above) that is either employed or seeking/available for employment, and is a key indicator tracked in India's PLFS, conducted by the National Statistical Office (NSO).

 

• The Economic Survey, tabled in Parliament a day before the Union Budget, is prepared under the guidance of the Chief Economic Adviser and reviews the state of the Indian economy over the preceding year.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The overall (male + female) LFPR in India has also shown a rising trend in recent PLFS rounds, partly attributed to rising rural female participation.

 

• The Economic Survey 2022-23 was presented ahead of the Union Budget 2023-24.

 

NOTE

 

• 55.1%, 59.3%, 54.2% (Options 1, 2, 3): These figures do not match the male LFPR for 2020-21 as reported in the Economic Survey 2022-23.

question: The Indian Constitution borrowed the concept of concurrent list from ______________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Australia.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The concept of the Concurrent List in the Indian Constitution was borrowed from the Australian Constitution. (समवर्ती सूची — ऑस्ट्रेलिया)

 

• The Seventh Schedule of the Indian Constitution divides legislative subjects into three lists — Union List, State List and Concurrent List — with the Concurrent List containing subjects on which both Parliament and State Legislatures can legislate.

 

• In case of a conflict between a Union law and a State law on a Concurrent List subject, the Union law generally prevails, subject to certain exceptions (Article 254).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• India's Constitution is often described as a 'bag of borrowings' — for example, Fundamental Rights were influenced by the USA, the Directive Principles of State Policy by Ireland, and the parliamentary system by the UK.

 

• The Concurrent List originally had 47 subjects (as per the 1950 Constitution) and now has more, following subsequent amendments (e.g., the 42nd Amendment moved subjects like Education and Forests from the State List to the Concurrent List).

 

NOTE

 

• Germany (Option 2): India borrowed the concept of the 'Emergency provisions' (suspension of Fundamental Rights during Emergency) from the Weimar Constitution of Germany, not the Concurrent List.

 

• USSR (Option 3): India borrowed the concept of Fundamental Duties and the ideals of socio-economic justice/Five-Year Plans inspiration from the USSR, not the Concurrent List.

 

• Japan (Option 4): India borrowed the concept of 'Procedure Established by Law' from the Japanese Constitution, not the Concurrent List.
